chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

You will not see the one you are waiting for until you become like the dead goat, for whom the lion does not care where it places its hand upon it. There is no honour for you to rise to, nor a supporter to whom you entrust your affairs.

key_terms.الَّذِي تَنْتَظِرُونَ: The one you are waiting for (referring to Al-Qa'im)

ai.seo_question: What condition must the companions meet before seeing the Awaited Imam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (as) critiques the spiritual passivity of his contemporaries, using the metaphor of the *muwat* (a dead goat left for scavengers) to illustrate their lack of dignity and agency. He emphasizes that merely waiting for the reappearance is insufficient; they must cultivate active worthiness (*sharaf*) and establish a firm spiritual foundation (*sinad*) to be worthy of the Imam's presence. This highlights the Shia emphasis on self-purification and readiness as prerequisites for witnessing the Mahdi.
